title: The ₹27,850-Crore 'Digital Arrest' Money Trail
dek: A single Goa woman's ₹2.6-crore 'digital arrest' scam complaint led the ED to a money-mule network that had moved ₹27,850 crore through dummy accounts and is linked to 163 FIRs across 20 states.

heroStat.label: in banking transactions traced through the mule-account network by the ED

promise.quote: India's banking and telecom systems will prevent organised networks from using dummy accounts and SIM cards to launder proceeds of cyber fraud at scale.
promise.madeBy: Banking-sector KYC framework and telecom SIM-verification norms
promise.role: Regulatory safeguard against mule-account and SIM-based cyber fraud
promise.context: A Goa resident was coerced by fraudsters posing as law-enforcement officials into transferring ₹2.60 crore between 21 May and 2 June 2025 into accounts falsely described as 'secret supervision accounts' — a scam pattern known as 'digital arrest'.

target.description: Bank accounts and SIM cards used for their disclosed, KYC-verified purpose, with anomalous high-volume transaction patterns flagged and blocked before mule networks can move crores through them.
target.standard: RBI KYC/anti-money-laundering norms and Department of Telecommunications SIM-verification rules.

reality.description: Investigating the Goa complaint, the ED's Panaji zonal office traced a nationwide network of dummy accounts and shell entities that had conducted banking transactions worth ₹27,850 crore and cash deposits of ₹2,904 crore. The bank accounts involved are linked to 163 FIRs and 330 complaints across 20 states and Union Territories, representing total reported victim losses of approximately ₹417.49 crore. The ED conducted searches at 20 premises in Mumbai and Goa on 17 July 2026, and further searches on 21 August 2026 that recovered ₹3.25 crore in cash. On 23 August 2026, the agency arrested two accused, Fahim Moin Hussain Sayed and Naim Mueen Sayyed, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

gap.metricLabel: Total money-trail transaction value traced vs. confirmed victim losses linked to FIRs
gap.note: The ₹27,850 crore figure reflects total transaction volume through the mule-account network, which investigators say handled proceeds from many frauds beyond the digital-arrest cases with confirmed FIRs; it should not be read as the total amount stolen from victims.

money.notes: ₹27,850 crore in transactions and ₹2,904 crore in cash deposits were traced through the network; ₹3.25 crore in cash was seized in the August 2026 raids.

timeline.label: Goa victim's funds transferred
timeline.detail: A Goa resident is coerced into transferring ₹2.60 crore into accounts described as 'secret supervision accounts' over roughly two weeks.

timeline.label: Cybercrime FIR registered
timeline.detail: North Goa cybercrime police register a case, which the ED later takes up under the PMLA.

timeline.detail: The ED conducts searches under PMLA Section 17 across Mumbai and Goa.

timeline.label: Further searches, cash seized
timeline.detail: Additional premises are searched; ₹3.25 crore in cash is recovered.

timeline.label: Two arrested
timeline.detail: The ED's Panaji zonal office arrests Fahim Moin Hussain Sayed and Naim Mueen Sayyed under Section 19 of the PMLA.

legalStatus.summary: This is a stub entry. Two individuals have been arrested under the PMLA; no chargesheet or trial outcome has been reported yet, and the network's organisers beyond those arrested have not been publicly identified in the sources reviewed.

keyIndividuals.outcome: Arrested by the ED on 23 August 2026 under Section 19 of the PMLA.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: a single digital-arrest complaint has uncovered a mule-account and shell-entity network of striking scale, illustrating how India's cyber-fraud epidemic is intertwined with organised money laundering. This is an active, fast-moving investigation with no resolution yet.
verdict.reasoning: This entry is based on reporting through late August 2026 covering the case's discovery, searches, and initial arrests. It has not yet been possible to verify how the ₹27,850 crore transaction figure was calculated or to identify the network's alleged masterminds.

incomplete: This is a stub entry; deeper research into the network's organisational structure and alleged masterminds is pending.
It is unclear whether the ₹27,850 crore transaction figure represents laundering of proceeds specifically from digital-arrest scams, or a broader mix of cyber-fraud types.
No chargesheet has been reported as of this entry's publication.
